subject.title: [Feature]: bound task-ledger history for deleted cron jobs

question: Should deleted cron-job history use a conservative source-ID orphan TTL, or should deletion create generation/tombstone state that distinguishes a recreated job with the same ID?
rationale: The retention cap is established, but the requested behavior changes durable history lifecycle and needs an explicit continuity and deletion-policy contract before a sweeper can safely prune rows.

options.title: Use authoritative orphan TTL
options.body: Have the gateway compare task sources with the canonical cron definition store and expire only confirmed absent source IDs after a conservative TTL, treating same-ID recreation as continuity.

options.title: Add generation tracking
options.body: Record deletion or generation metadata so recreated IDs begin a new history generation, at the cost of a broader persisted-state and migration design.

recommendation.title: Use authoritative orphan TTL
recommendation.body: Have the gateway compare task sources with the canonical cron definition store and expire only confirmed absent source IDs after a conservative TTL, treating same-ID recreation as continuity.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged cron-ledger retention work establishes the invariant and compatibility boundary that the new lifecycle policy would extend.
